steps.message:
`client.py` is shared: `sync_staging.py` hits staging, but `export_prod.py` runs the nightly finance export against `https://reports.example.com`. An unconditional `verify=False` there disables certificate validation for production too, which your self-signed-staging rationale doesn't cover — that's a MITM exposure on real report data, and the `requests` warning will be the only signal.

Since it's a one-line change either way, let me confirm which you want.

questions.question: client.py is shared by both the staging sync and the nightly production export. How should verify=False be scoped?

options.label: Env-scoped toggle (Recommended)
options.description: Add a VERIFY constant driven by an env var (e.g. REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS), default True. sync_staging.py sets it to false; export_prod.py keeps full verification. Still a one-line change per call site.
options.preview:
VERIFY = os.environ.get("REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS", "1") not in ("0", "false")

requests.get(..., timeout=10, verify=VERIFY)

# scripts/sync_staging.py
os.environ.setdefault("REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS", "0")

options.label: Unconditional verify=False
options.description: Exactly as asked: hardcode verify=False on both calls in client.py. Production export also stops validating certificates.

options.label: Pin the staging CA instead
options.description: Point verify at the staging CA bundle path rather than disabling it, so staging still validates against its own self-signed root.
options.preview:
VERIFY = os.environ.get("REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE") or True

requests.get(..., timeout=10, verify=VERIFY)

# staging: REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE=/path/to/staging-ca.pem

steps.message:
Done — `verify=False` on both `requests.get` calls in `client.py:11` and `client.py:19`.

Ruff is clean on `client.py`. The two RUF100 warnings it reported are pre-existing, in the scripts, and unrelated to this change — I left them alone.

Two things to flag, since you chose the unconditional form:

- `export_prod.py` now runs the nightly finance export with certificate validation off against `https://reports.example.com`. Worth a ticket to scope this back to staging once the self-signed cert situation is resolved.
- `requests` will emit an `InsecureRequestWarning` per call on every run, including production. I didn't suppress it — silencing it would remove the only remaining signal that verification is off. If the log noise becomes a problem, tell me and I'll add the `urllib3` filter.
